provenance.method: Question created for the Relationships & family UK v1 bounded coverage slice from reviewed first-party/specialist routes and existing governed Concepts; it preserves uncertainty and does not create personalised relationship, diagnostic, legal or safeguarding authority.

question: How can partners talk about processing time, communication style and sensory needs?
why_it_matters: Partners can misread delayed responses, direct language, need for written communication, routine or sensory limits as indifference or rejection when the underlying needs have not been made explicit.
current_understanding: A useful governed route is to describe concrete interaction needs rather than using a diagnostic label as a complete explanation: for example needing more time before answering, preferring written follow-up, agreeing how to signal overload, or discussing shared-space sensory needs. Both people still have their own boundaries and preferences. ND Oracle does not decide compatibility or who is right.
evidence_needed: Relationship research that compares mutually agreed communication adaptations across different neurotypes.
More evidence about sensory and executive-function accommodations in close relationships without assuming one partner must do all adapting.
reopening_conditions: New high-quality relationship evidence supports a more specific intervention claim.
Existing guidance changes materially or proves too one-sided.
dissent: Neurodivergence can shape communication, but it does not explain every relationship difficulty or remove either person's responsibility for respectful behaviour.
